Subject: RE: MedHealth asks re: BAA / subprocessors / transfers

Marissa / team —

Looping in a quick internal summary and recommended next steps from Legal & Compliance. High level: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads but with a few documented controls and an execution path.

Key points:
- BAA: Redwood will execute a BAA. We require minimal operational guardrails: (a) customer must identify the scope of PHI processing; (b) do not permit training models on PHI unless explicitly contracted and isolated; (c) logging/audit retention aligned with SLA (we can negotiate retention windows).

- Hosting modes: Hosted API (our standard shared-hosted tier) can process PHI if the customer accepts the standard BAA plus specific technical controls (customer KMS for key separation recommended). For higher-assurance customers we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated capacity.

- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): Supported via our KMS integration for Dedicated/Private and limited support on Hosted through envelope encryption. Full BYOK (HSM-backed) is available for Dedicated/Private deployments — we should propose that in the commercial terms.

- Subprocessors: We'll provide the current roster (see attached CSV). We do not proactively limit all future subprocessors in the base DPA but we offer a contractual commit to notify customers and provide a 30-day window for material additions; for enterprise deals we can negotiate approval rights or a restricted subprocessor list as a contract addendum (typical for sensitive health customers).

- International transfers: We have EU regions; if MedHealth requires data residency we can route requests to EU region endpoints for storage and inference. For cross-border processing we rely on SCCs + documented safeguards; we can add a clause for data localization where feasible.

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and a pen test summary are available under NDA — we'll share in the next message.

Timeline & next steps:
1) I will attach: subprocessor roster (current as of 2026-02-12) and a HIPAA addendum template.
2) Legal will prepare a draft BAA/DPA redline that reflects the above and highlights BYOK options and subprocessor notification. Estimate 7–10 business days for an initial redline.
3) Recommend scheduling a 30–45 minute call between Redwood Legal/Infosec (Neha, Vivek) and MedHealth InfoSec + Procurement next week to clarify scope and key terms. Aditya / Marissa to propose times.

Risks/notes:
- If MedHealth requires strict prohibition on future subprocessors without prior consent, expect additional negotiation time — this is typically handled in enterprise addenda.
- If MedHealth insists on model training on PHI, that requires separate technical isolation and compliance review (we do not allow training on customer PHI in shared models).

Attachments: Subprocessors_2026-02-12.csv; HIPAA_Addendum_Template_2026-02-12.docx
